newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA SAYS DOESN'T RECOMMEND BIDDING AT 2006 AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: MERITA SAYS DOESN'T RECOMMEND BIDDING AT 2006 AUCTION.

text.p: Merita Bank said it does not recommend bidding in Thursday's auction of 2006 bonds as it expects to see higher yield levels at which to buy the paper.
"On a 1-2 months horizon the 2006 remains attractive but we expect to see higher (yield) levels at which to buy the bond," Merita said in a pre-auction comment dated November 21.
It said German Bunds were expected to trade sideways over the coming weeks, and the Finnish bond market was likely to track Bunds.
"Given the fall in domestic trading volumes, the Finnish market is expected to track even more closely the Bund market," Merita said.
"However, it cannot be excluded that the traditionally increased liquidity of life insurance funds towards the very end of the year could support the Finnish bond market," it added.

The auction results are due after 1330/1030 GMT. In the previous auction on October 10, the State Treasury raised 1.5 billion markka at a yield of 6.42 percent. The STO has said it will issue at most 1.5 billion markka in today's auction.
